hypotheses.rationale: Validation loss exhibits large oscillations and occasional increases after epoch ~7‑8 while training loss continues to drop, a pattern typical of overfitting when LoRA training runs far beyond convergence. The default 18 epochs is higher than needed for this task.

Training loss steadily declines to near‑zero, yet validation loss jumps between very low and high values across epochs, indicating the validation set does not mirror the training distribution, causing noisy validation signals.
The unstable validation loss resembles label noise: similar inputs receive conflicting intents in BANKING77, leading to inconsistent gradients and fluctuating validation performance.

hypotheses.location: chat template used in training vs inference
hypotheses.rationale: If the training chat template differs from the one used at inference, the model may sometimes correctly follow the format (low loss) and sometimes ignore it (high loss), producing the observed validation loss swings.

A LoRA rank of 16 might be insufficient to capture the full intent‑classification variability, causing the model to stall; however the occasional very low validation loss suggests this is less likely than the above issues.
